newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle calls range mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle calls range mixed.

text.p: Early calls on CME live cattle futures ranged from 0.100 cent per lb higher to 0.200 lower while feeder cattle futures were called 0.100 cent higher to 0.100 lower, livestock analysts said.

Bull spreading was expected to support the nearby live cattle contract as most months are expected to trend lower following Friday's USDA Cattle-on-Feed Report. The report was called neutral to slightly bearish with the overall cattle on feed number considered bearish for back months, they said.
Cattle markets were seen coming under pressure later as larger numbers of fed cattle come to market, they said.

Cash cattle prices may hold this week as feedlots appeared current and any carryover of showlists consisted of mostly "green" cattle needing extra days on feed. But a weak tone to the cash wholesale boxed beef market may also counter any strength in cash cattle, they said.

Feeder cattle indications ranged mixed with a higher index considered supportive while expected pressure in deferred live cattle futures was cited for pressure. The market is vulnerable to weakness in live cattle, they added.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.27 to $77.64 per cwt, the highest level since August 23, 1994.
